paragraphs.en: Here's a {riddle} : What do {traffic} {jams} , long {lines} and {waiting} for a {vacation} to start all have in {common} ? There is one answer.They're all {situations} where we could use a little {extra} {patience} .
paragraphs.cn: 有这样一个 <u> 谜题 </u> ： <u> 交通堵塞 </u> 、排长 <u> 队 </u> 和 <u> 等待假期 </u> 开始，这三者有什么 <u> 共同 </u> 点？答案只有一个。在这些 <u> 情况 </u> 下，我们都需要 <u> 多 </u> 一点 <u> 耐心 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: In the {Digital} Age, we're used to having what we need {immediately} and right at our {fingertips} .However, research suggests that if we practiced patience, we'd be a {whole} lot better off.Just as a {sculpture} takes time to shape, only those who wait long enough can reveal the {essence} of life.Here are several {tricks} .
paragraphs.cn: 在这个 <u> 数字 </u> 时代，我们习惯于动动 <u> 手指 </u> 就能 <u> 马上 </u> 获得我们需要的一切。然而，研究表明，如果我们能培养耐心，我们的生活就会好很多。正如 <u> 雕塑 </u> 需要时间来成形一样，只有那些等待时间足够长的人才能揭示生活的 <u> 真谛 </u> 。这里有几个 <u> 诀窍 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: A messy space leads to a confused mind, making it difficult to remain calm during stressful situations.For instance, before rushing through a busy {airport} , you should organize your {wallet} and make sure all the important documents such as your {cash} , {passport} and ID {card} are in order.
paragraphs.cn: 杂乱的空间会导致思维混乱，在压力大的情况下很难让人保持冷静。例如，匆忙穿过繁忙的 <u> 机场 </u> 之前，你应该整理好你的 <u> 钱包 </u> ，确保所有重要文件，如 <u> 现金 </u> 、 <u> 护照 </u> 和身份 <u> 证 </u> 都井然有序。

paragraphs.en: Take time to contemplate ( (沉思) ) and practice {gratitude}
paragraphs.cn: 花时间沉思并践行 <u> 感恩 </u> 之情

paragraphs.en: Setting aside time each day, perhaps during {noon} or in the evening, to light a {candle} and focus on your breath.It can also help us {foster} patience and become {thankful} for our lives.This practice can be as simple as saying“ {thank} you” to the {host} when you have a good time, for example.Research shows that thankfulness makes us happier, less stressed and even more {optimistic} .
paragraphs.cn: 每天留出时间，也许是 <u> 中午 </u> ，也许是晚上，点一根 <u> 蜡烛 </u> ，专注于你的呼吸。这也有助于我们 <u> 培养 </u> 耐心，并对生活心怀 <u> 感激 </u> 。这种做法可以像你度过了愉快的时光时对 <u> 主人 </u> 说“ <u> 谢谢 </u> ”一样简单。研究表明，感恩让我们更快乐、压力更小，甚至更 <u> 乐观 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: {Instant} gratification ( (满足) ) may seem like the most “feel good” {option} at the time, but {psychology} research suggests waiting for things {actually} makes us happier in the long run.Start with small {tasks} .Put off watching your favorite show {until} the {weekend} or wait 10 extra minutes before going for that {cake} .When waiting for a friend who is running late, use the opportunity to read a {brochure} or take a {bus} to nearby shops, turning the delay into a productive time.You'll soon find that the more patience you practice, the more you {start} to {apply} it to other, more {annoying} {occasions} .
paragraphs.cn: <u> 即时 </u> 满足在当时看来可能是最“感觉良好”的 <u> 选择 </u> ，但 <u> 心理学 </u> 研究表明，从长远来看，等待 <u> 实际上 </u> 会让我们更快乐。从小的 <u> 任务 </u> 开始。把最喜欢的节目推迟 <u> 到周末 </u> 再看，或者享用 <u> 蛋糕 </u> 之前多等上10分钟。在等待迟到的朋友时，利用这个机会阅读一本 <u> 小册子 </u> 或坐 <u> 公共汽车 </u> 去附近的商店，把耽搁的时间变成富有成效的时间。你很快就会发现，你培养的耐心越多，你就越能 <u> 开始 </u> 把它 <u> 应用 </u> 到其他更 <u> 烦人的场合 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: So many of us have the {belief} that being {comfortable} is the only {state} we will {tolerate} , and when we experience something outside of our {comfort} {zone} , we get {impatient} about the circumstances.You should learn to say to yourself,“This is {merely} uncomfortable, not {intolerable} .”You'll then {gradually} become more {patient} .
paragraphs.cn: 我们有许多人都 <u> 相信 </u> ， <u> 舒适 </u> 是我们唯一能 <u> 容忍 </u> 的 <u> 状态 </u> ，而当我们经历 <u> 舒适区 </u> 之外的事情时，我们就会对这类情况感到 <u> 不耐烦 </u> 。你应该学会对自己说：“这 <u> 只是 </u> 令人有些不舒服，并非 <u> 无法忍受 </u> 。”这样你就会 <u> 逐渐 </u> 变得更 <u> 有耐心 </u> 。 MKqjwFu4arM4cgPc+LiB66EBg/AaE0u6XBr6IpfU5EiRRdX6Ad+uTD+Kdly4W5UG
